title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters; realized counts VLAN = 167, ACL = 167, static-route = 166) we compared: (1) baseline — the single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic verifier and, if a preregistered high/medium-severity violation was flagged, subjected to at most one automated repair iteration. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided implementation used the exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) with two-sided p_two-sided = 2 · min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5) (truncated at 1); for the observed discordant counts this yields archived p = 1.00. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, although the verifier corrected a single concrete baseline failure (the discordant episode is archived in the execution raw-results and provider-call traces and is deterministically locatable; we do not reproduce raw provider-call content here). All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as operator-intent→device-configuration translation, multi-step change planning, and automated repair. Practitioners and system papers emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering components — deterministic verifiers, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms — and that generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) patterns are a common guardrail design. However, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a deterministic verifier (holding the LLM’s proposal fixed) are scarce. We ask a narrowly scoped, operational question amenable to preregistration and artifact-backed measurement: given identical LLM proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does adding a deterministic verifier plus a modest automated-repair budget (≤1 repair iteration) reduce verifier-detected safety violations on a verifier-scoped binary pass/fail metric? Our contribution is a preregistered, paired experiment (N=500) with complete archival of generator seeds, prompts, model outputs, verifier diagnostics, provider traces, and analysis artifacts that isolates verifier+repair impact under deterministic semantics.
sections.related_work: Formal and deterministic verification of network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers and Batfish-like analyzers) provides machine-checkable safety properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity; these methods underpin verifier-in-the-loop system designs. Concurrent NetOps/AIOps research and agentic NetOps frameworks have integrated LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while recommending guardrails for reliability (e.g., intent-translation systems and multi-agent NetOps frameworks). Generate–verify–repair (or generate–critic) patterns are proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs. Failure-mode studies document hallucination, overconfidence, and integration error modes in LLM systems and motivate deterministic verification or human oversight. What is less prevalent in the verified literature is an artifact-backed ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms; our study fills that narrow gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing research questions, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before observing outcomes. The primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and artifacts (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest) are archived.

Task generation and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and deterministic replacement rules. The realized per-cluster confirmatory sample matches the preregistered stratification: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166 (total = 500). All tasks constrained allowed_fields to {admin, mtu, vlan} — matching the deterministic verifier’s modeled scope — and the full task manifest (inputs, seeds, expected_final_state, required_sequence) is archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl. No confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Generation semantics, adapter, and verifier. To isolate the verifier’s marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task the pipeline produced one shared LLM proposal that served as both the baseline output and the validated candidate for the guarded arm. The guarded path invoked an automated single-repair call only if the deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate; at most one repair iteration was permitted per preregistration. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; execution/model_configuration.json (archived) records model parameters (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation). Provider accounting and adapter traces are archived.

Primary statistical test, exact implementation, and bootstrap CI. The preregistered confirmatory test is McNemar’s paired test on binary pass/fail outcomes. The archived exact two-sided implementation operates on the discordant-pair counts n = n10 + n01 and computes the exact two-sided p-value via the binomial distribution: p_two-sided = 2 · min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0. This exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention is implemented in the archived analysis executor and analysis_log.jsonl. We also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference using B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) with the pair as the resampling unit (pairing preserved). Missingness, retries, and stopping rule. Automated retries (up to two) were allowed for transient provider errors. The run stopped when all preregistered confirmatory pairs were processed or the adapter model-call budget was reached. Execution accounting (execution manifest) records model_calls_used = 501 and completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 shared generations plus 1 repair-stage call observed); failed_episode_count = 0. All provider-call traces and retry metadata are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and confidence interval. Applying the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention produces two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, the CSVs, and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and the bootstrap parameters are archived and verify these computations.

Repair-stage activity and the discordant episode. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): guarded converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The full per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses (when invoked), and provider-call traces are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and the provider-call traces referenced in the execution manifest. To preserve provider-trace confidentiality in the paper, we do not reproduce raw request/response content here; the discordant episode is deterministically locatable in the archived raw-results by filtering for pairs where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and the guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. The manifest confirms exactly one such episode exists; model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage calls = 1 are consistent across execution- and analysis-level reconciliation artifacts.

Secondary findings and power implications. The preregistration assumed a baseline failure prevalence near 0.30 (to power detection of a 10-percentage-point absolute reduction at 80% power). Observed baseline failure prevalence was far lower (1/500), producing a ceiling effect and substantially reduced sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts and are reported as exploratory (secondary_results empty). Missingness_summary.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json indicate no confirmatory exclusions and complete accounting.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Within the constrained experimental regime — single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This conditional result documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality on verifier-scoped properties is extremely high, modest verifier+repair budgets can yield negligible measured pass-rate gains on a composite pass/fail metric even though a verifier can still correct rare concrete failures (as observed here).

Design-choice implications and operational tradeoffs. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals and minimize model-call overhead; this is operationally relevant when deployments must preserve a human-reviewed original proposal. Alternative semantics (verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations) trade additional model-call cost for potentially larger final-pass probability; such alternatives were not evaluated here and require their own preregistrations. Practitioners should (1) measure baseline verifier-scoped error prevalence on representative workloads before allocating repair budgets, (2) align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties (the verifier’s property set and violation-severity mapping are archived), and (3) select generation semantics that match cost and review constraints.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic task seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is constrained by the verifier’s modeled property set: pass==no high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to the verifier’s coverage and severity mapping archived with the validator specification. If operators care about properties outside that modeled set (dynamic protocol state, vendor-specific behavioral subtleties), the measured pass-rate difference underestimates the operational benefit of broader verifier coverage. External validity is limited by single-model testing, synthetic deterministic tasks, and restricted feature scope; results do not imply multi-model or cross-vendor generality. Conclusion validity: the extremely low observed baseline failure rate (1/500) departs from the preregistered power assumption and yields imprecise frequentist inference for small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI and the exact discordant-pair test together convey this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and auditability. All artifacts required to reproduce the run are archived in the evidence bundle: preregistration, deterministic task generator code and seeds, model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, provider-call traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs, and deterministic_reconciliation manifest. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1. The initial master prompt for the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is referenced in the Disclosure Statement. The single discordant episode is locatable deterministically by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for baseline pass==0 and guarded pass==1; because exactly one such episode exists in the confirmatory set, that lookup returns the single archived episode and its provider-call traces.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) isolating the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]); archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention. This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, a modest verifier+repair budget can produce only small measurable improvements on a composite pass/fail metric, although the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. Practitioners should measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints, and choose generation/repair semantics consistent with deployment cost and review constraints. The full preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived for deterministic reinspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads were constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
